rows.subtype: Not arguing with the confused mind [Response]
rows.description: A caregiver avoids correcting or quarrelling about facts that the person cannot hold, and responds to the feeling behind the words instead. Reassurance, routine and a calm environment reduce distress.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: A family that notices memory, judgment or personality changes seeks a doctor's assessment early instead of assuming it is only old age. Early understanding helps with safety planning, legal matters and support.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: A toddler seeks lap, hugs and carrying to feel safe, and becomes distressed or withdrawn when comfort is missing. Warm touch is not spoiling; it helps build calm and trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, detachment, calm, trust

rows.subtype: Child seeking cuddles after a bad day [Actor]
rows.description: A young child who has been scolded, scared or tired climbs into a lap wordlessly. Accepting the hug first and talking later teaches the child that closeness is available when things go wrong.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, fear, tiredness

rows.description: A teenager may stiffen at family hugs and want personal space while still craving warmth. Respecting their pace, offering a pat or sitting beside them, and keeping the option open keeps connection alive.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Homesick and touch-starved in a hostel [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult far from family may feel an aching loneliness, missing the casual hug or a hand on the shoulder. Friends, pets, sport and caring routines can meet some of that need in healthy ways.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: affection, loneliness, nostalgia

rows.description: A person living alone may feel restless, low and unusually sensitive after weeks without any friendly touch or company. Wanting comfort is human, and safe ways to meet it include friends, family and community.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: boredom, loneliness, trust

rows.description: A caring person asks before hugging, accepts a no without offence and finds other ways to show warmth. Touch is comforting only when it is welcome, and some people's histories or cultures shape their comfort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young child begins to link feelings to body sensations such as butterflies, hot face or heavy legs. Adults who name these signals help the child understand what is going on inside.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Missing hunger or the need for the toilet [Actor]
rows.description: A child absorbed in play may ignore hunger, thirst or a full bladder until it becomes urgent, then suddenly falls apart. Pausing for a quick body check builds awareness over time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
